homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym and T composes no other entity under DAIL's name. The reached kind is a collision (Capture Registry, per_dim.reached 'collision'): the composition reads the descriptive name as a kind and lists DAIL first among four records of AI litigation, the other three distinct entities with names of their own. etidail.com (card 4) carries DAIL's own name and is an address of the entity, recorded as such. 'DAIL' is matched case-sensitively in the archive's string pass so that the Irish Dáil does not enter; neither the field nor the census names it.
distinct_entities: Fisher & Phillips LLP's AI Litigation Tracker (B2, card 2), a law firm's tracker of U.S. AI litigation since 25 February 2021: a distinct record of the same kind
Damien Charlotin's AI Hallucination Cases Database (B3, card 3), a researcher's database of decisions finding hallucinated content: a distinct record, of decisions only
Hogan Lovells Cadwalader's AI Litigation Case Law Tracker (B5, card 5), a law firm's global AI case law tracker: a distinct record, holding authorship and inventorship matters of its own (F29–F32)

the Ethical Tech Initiative, DAIL's operator (F1, F2), an interdisciplinary collaboration distinct from the database; George Washington University, whose site and footer carry it (F10), an institution distinct from both; 'George Washington University Law School', named by T and on no saved page (CAP-1-05)
the companion database of issued opinions (F6), a record held beside DAIL, unread

Thaler v. Perlmutter, the case through which the human-authorship requirement was settled (#195), and Thaler's UK inventorship appeal (F31): litigation, distinct from any record of it; no source says DAIL holds either
the archive's court of record, r.30 THE RUBY MOOT (#193), and its Docket No. 1 (#823): the archive's own record of authorship disputes, distinct from DAIL

Neighbours in the census (rows composed the same day under the same brief, paths not checked here): Copyright and Artificial Intelligence (the U.S. Copyright Office, copyright-office-ai) and the Authors Guild's Human Authored Certification (authors-guild-human-authored), the census's other governance rows

captures.description: THE NAME, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The primary dedicated public resources and trackers for artificial intelligence litigation include:' Four bullets: 'DAIL – The Database of AI Litigation: Maintained by George Washington University Law School's Ethical Tech Initiative, this resource covers ongoing and completed AI-related cases starting from the initial complaint onward—regardless of whether they produce published decisions.'; Damien Charlotin's AI Hallucination Cases Database; Fisher Phillips's AI Litigation Tracker; Hogan Lovells's case law tracker. Five cards: GW Blogs, Fisher Phillips, Damien Charlotin, etidail.com, Hogan Lovells Cadwalader.
